name: Transcendence of pi settles squaring the circle (Lindemann)
summary: Lindemann's proof that pi is transcendental implied no ruler-and-compass squaring of the circle, resolving a geometric problem by an algebraic argument.

name: Geometric (Clifford) algebra
summary: Clifford fused Hamilton's quaternions and Grassmann's exterior algebra into a single geometric algebra.

name: Cardinality meets dimension: R^n equinumerous with R
summary: Cantor defined equivalence of sets by bijection and showed that Euclidean n-space has the same cardinality as the line, which forced dimension to be defined by something finer than counting points.

name: Logicism: reducing arithmetic to logic (Frege, Russell, Whitehead)
summary: Frege tried to base arithmetic on logic alone; Russell's paradox shook this and Russell and Whitehead's Principia used a theory of types to avoid it.

name: Automorphic functions and uniformisation
summary: Poincare and Klein linked discrete groups of Mobius transformations, hyperbolic geometry and differential equations, and uniformised algebraic curves.

name: Class field theory
summary: Abelian extensions of number fields were matched to ideal-class-type groups, from Kronecker, Weber and Hilbert through Takagi's existence theorem and Artin's reciprocity law.

name: Vector analysis
summary: Gibbs and Heaviside extracted vector methods from quaternions.

name: Weil's dictionary: number fields, function fields, Riemann surfaces
summary: A three-way analogy between number fields, function fields over finite fields and compact Riemann surfaces transfers statements and methods between arithmetic and geometry.

name: Combinatorial group theory from topology and geometry
summary: Presentations by generators and relations arose from geometric studies of discrete groups, then Poincare's fundamental group, Tietze's transformations and the Dehn and Nielsen-Schreier line made group presentations a topological tool.

name: Differential Galois theory
summary: Picard and Vessiot carried the Galois correspondence to linear differential equations, with Lie groups replacing finite groups.
